doc.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Big bands at the Paramount and Strand theaters
summary: Gibbs learned music from the stage shows at the Paramount, not just radio, and was thrilled by Benny Goodman's 'Let's Dance'; working with him later, he found Goodman a 'foggy idiot' who could play clarinet.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: The music of the day, when you were a youngster, radio was extremely important, right?
Is that where you got most of your exposure?

Well no, they had the big bands at the Paramount Theater and the Strand Theater. Never in my born days did I ever think I would ever work with Benny Goodman. When I was a kid I’d be the first one in line, five or six o’clock in the morning, to get in the Paramount Theater. And when that stage would go up in the old days, and people would go to the Paramount Theater, that stage used to rise. And while it was going up from the pit, Benny would be playing the theme song “Let’s Dance.” My hair would stand up. And that was one of my favorite bands. And then when I got to work with him, it was amazing. And then when I got to work with him I found out what an idiot he was. Complete foggy idiot. But he could play the clarinet.
